plain: A wicker basket by the radiator with a folded blanket in it. The blanket is still warm. Somebody has just left.
lines: {cat} looks at the basket, looks at you, and climbs in. She turns round twice and sits down, perfectly content.
Erwin Schrödinger lived in Dublin from 1939 to 1956 and worked at the Institute for Advanced Studies.
His cat in a box was only a thought experiment, from 1935, to show how odd one idea in physics sounds at cat size.
Is she in the basket until you look? You look. She is. She was always going to be.
{cat} sits down in the lane and looks at you, and then she is not there. The grin is.
It hangs at about cat height for as long as it takes to notice. Then it goes too, and she is back, washing a paw.
Lewis Carroll was born at Daresbury, in Cheshire, in 1832. Grinning like a Cheshire cat is a good deal older than Alice.
A dusty cabinet at the back. The marquee says MONSTERQUEST in letters that were once red, and the coin slot is taped over.
It does not take coins. It is on anyway, glowing faintly, with nobody at the stick.
HIGH SCORES. 1. JIM ... 999999. The other nine lines are blank, and look like they have been waiting a long time.
A scrap of squared paper under a pencil, in neat capitals: SXW WKH NHWWOH RQ.
Pinned beside it: 'J. Caesar, three along. Suetonius says he did it for his private letters.' Someone is having fun.

right_lines: Shift each letter back three: S to P, X to U, W to T. PUT THE KETTLE ON. Best code you have ever broken.
You pocket the slip. Whoever wrote it wanted to be kind, in a way nobody else could read.
wrong_lines: That does not fit the letters. S back three is P, not the one you picked. Try again.

done: The slip says PUT THE KETTLE ON, three letters along. The paper on the table has been replaced with a fresh one that says the same.

ring: A phone box nearby rings once, loud in the quiet, and then waits like something that heard you coming.
answer: A calm recorded voice: 'At the third stroke, it will be {time} precisely.' Pip. Pip. Pip.
That is an hour fast. The pips are perfect. The hour is between the box and its conscience.

lines: A phone box on the corner. A card is taped inside the glass: 'Question wanted. Answer already in: 42. Reward: tea.'
Douglas Adams was born in Cambridge in 1952 and studied at St John's. He said 42 was a joke, an ordinary smallish number he chose.
You check your pockets, in case a question has been left in one.
Somebody has sat down at the far end of the bench. You did not see them arrive, which is how benches work.
'Tower's from 1894,' they say, watching the lamps come on. 'Copied from the one in Paris. Half the height, but it has got a ballroom.'
They nod, as if that settled it, and get up and go.

bagpuss: {name}, is it? There was a saggy old cloth cat on the telly when I was small, and I cried when it finished.
She is not saggy, mind. Not a bit. Lovely name.
schrodinger: {name}? The one with the box, is it? Well, she is not in the box. She is on my good chair.
That is the only fact I need.
macavity: {name}? There is a poem about a cat with that name, by T. S. Eliot. Never there when the trouble starts.
Funny. She will be at the bowl at six, and she will have an alibi.

lines: A second slip is folded in behind the first, in a different hand, damp but legible.
'Re your request for soap: sent. The Avon runs into the Severn, so you may find it. Please do not send it back.'
